newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Dominican Rep. to import food to head off protests.
newsitem.headline: Dominican Rep. to import food to head off protests.

text.p: The Dominican government on Tuesday announced a programme to import food in the face of threatened mass protests over rising prices.

After meeting with President Leonel Fernandez, Agriculture Minister Frank Rodriguez announced that the government would import beans, rice, potatoes and chickens, key items in the Dominican diet that have been in short supply.
A protest group, the Collective of Popular Organisations, has threatened more demonstrations this week to demand measures to lower the cost of living and public works projects to generate new jobs.
The group has staged several strikes in recent weeks, and at least one turned violent, leaving a police officer dead and several people wounded.

Government officials have dismissed the strikes as politically motivated actions engineered by opposition parties. The government is discussing an agreement with leaders of the popular organisations and trade unions to avoid a general strike.
